title: Lust and chastity
hookLine: chastity means love that respects people, whether single or married
tomorrow: works of mercy for the body

lines: A LOOK, A QUESTION, A SUMMONS.
cards: Evening in Jerusalem, in the season when kings go out to battle. But King David has stayed home.
He gets up from his bed and walks on the palace roof, and from there he sees a woman bathing, "and the woman was very beautiful to look upon."
The next words are quiet and terrible: "David sent and enquired after the woman." He learns her name, Bathsheba. He learns she is married, to one of his own soldiers, away at the war.
And he sends for her anyway. A look, then a question, then a summons.

teach.b: Notice how the story moves. David doesn't start with a crime. He starts with a look, and the look becomes a plan, and the plan treats Bathsheba as something a king can send for.
In the whole scene she barely speaks. She is acted upon. That's the heart of what Christian teaching means by lust.
Not desire itself: the Bible celebrates desire, and gives a whole book, the Song of Songs, to lovers longing for each other.
Lust is desire that turns a person into a thing to be used. Jesus takes it inward, to the look: "whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart."
Chastity is the answer, and it's more than a no.

In Christian teaching it's for everyone: for someone single, churches teach it as waiting; for someone married, as faithfulness to one person. Either way, the root is love that respects the whole person.

Because of the Bible's first page: "God created man in his own image." In Christian teaching, every person you see carries that image. And Paul tells the Corinthians, "your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost."
Not a thing. A temple. Christians differ on many questions about sex and marriage, and churches teach different things on some of them.
But the lines from Genesis and from Paul point one way: a person is never an object. And David's story doesn't end on the roof. The prophet Nathan comes to him later, and David hears what he's done.

how: Christian churches teach chastity as a virtue for everyone: for single people as abstaining from sex outside marriage, and for married people as faithfulness to one spouse; Christian teaching on the deadly sins pairs lust with chastity.

games.q: you're King David on the palace roof. you've seen a woman bathing, and you're told she is Bathsheba, the wife of one of your soldiers at the war. what do you do?
o: go back inside and leave her be.
ask her husband to come home.
games.why: David sends for her. a look, then a question, then a summons. the prophet Nathan later confronts him with what he has done.

practice: Bring to mind a few people you'll see or scroll past today, a coworker, a stranger on the street, someone on a screen, and for each one slowly add what you can't see: a mother somewhere, a bad night, a favorite song, a name.
Let each one become a whole life, not a picture. If you pray, you can hold Genesis in mind: made in the image of God.

wordCard.voice: Lust and chastity. Desire that uses a person, and love that respects the whole person, whether single or married.

orig.note: Greek: purity, chastity. The word in 1 Timothy 4:12, be an example in purity.

carryVoice: Your line: people, not things. In Christian teaching, every face carries that image. See you soon.
